about: The strategic atlas of Westernesse's reference worlds (doc/architecture/mission-22/world/orientation.md): what certain countries are, as facts the lower generators read, written by hand, for the worlds whose seeds are listed (`worlds`), each world drawing the same countries with its own detail. A country stands at a cell of the grid (`cell`, the first country 0,0; north is minus y), and says its name, its kind of country, its majority people and faith (given to the Deem `region` generator as the Great Desert gives its terrain), the side its land falls to the sea, the arts of the makers whose works are in it, what its settlements live by (by what lies around them, as Livelihoods reads a terrain's), the names of its chief settlements (the first its seat), and its facts: polity, who rules it and from where, its people's number, what it lives by, is short of and sells, its dangers, its roads and its neighbours, written into its module as Kyr facts. A world not listed is drawn as before. Read by src/world/strategic-atlas.ts.

facts.polity: the Rì's southern march, kept for the Rì by a reeve at Porthalen
facts.people: some six thousand: fifteen hundred in Porthalen, the rest in the fen villages and the hamlets on the sea-bank
facts.lives: salt boiled in pans on the shore, eels, reed, charcoal from the ridge
facts.short: fuel for the pans, iron, and grain in a wet year
facts.sells: salt, up the drove road to Brynach and north to the city
facts.danger: the tides and the old sea-gates that hold them, the fen, and the customs-men on the drove road
facts.works: the Water-Wardens' sea-gates and cisterns, which keep the fen dry still, the last of them failing

facts.polity: the Rì's own country, ruled from the Llys in Dun Rìerdan, the city of the seven powers
facts.people: some forty thousand: twenty thousand in the city, the rest in two market towns and the villages of the river
facts.lives: the court, the colleges and the guilds of the city, timber and wool from the river country
facts.sells: learning, law, licences and coin: whatever the seven powers grant
facts.danger: debt and the law in the city, and footpads on the roads in
facts.works: the Star-Readers' towers, under the city's own

facts.polity: a lordship of the fells, whose lord owes the Rì a war-band and will not pay the Rì's toll on the drove road
facts.people: some four thousand: a walled market at the pass, iron-pit villages, and shielings on the high pasture
facts.lives: iron from the pits, wool, and cattle driven down the drove road to the fen and the city
facts.danger: the dragon on the high pasture, wolves, and winter on the tops
facts.works: the Delvers' galleries under the fells
